cases.note: Observed on podman 5.8.1 (rootless, libkrun machine, arm64). The baseline keeps running. With all capabilities dropped the container exits with status 1 (su: can't set groups). Adding back only CAP_SETUID still exits with status 1 (can't set groups). Adding back only CAP_SETGID still exits with status 1 (setuid: Operation not permitted). Both together keep it running, so no single capability resolves it.

Observed on podman 5.8.1 (rootless, libkrun machine, arm64). The baseline keeps running. With a read-only root filesystem and a writable /tmp the container exits with status 1 (Read-only file system). Adding a writable tmpfs at /var/lib keeps it running.

Does not manifest as a treatment failure on podman 5.8.1 (rootless, libkrun machine, arm64). There the sysctl net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start is 1024 inside the container, so the baseline run already exits with status 1 (nc: bind: Permission denied) and the baseline gate makes EXEC-02 UNVERIFIED with reason BASELINE_FAILED. Dropping all capabilities changes nothing, and dropping all and adding only CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE makes the listener start. expected_minimal records that capability as the nominal cause, and the case is left out of the accuracy denominator. An engine that lowers the sysctl to 0 would let the baseline run, but no such engine was available here and that outcome is unverified.
